notes_for_editor: Wikipedia and a commercial travel site were used for leads only. Current condition of the tower is not described by any source read (Wikipedia, citing Lighthouse Digest, says it has deteriorated severely); Today section deliberately silent. Metz's 1901 report is quoted via LighthouseFriends, not read in the original. The Bulletin 1919 rescue date is garbled in OCR ('April 2'); LighthouseFriends gives 28 April. Bulletin 1926 storm: only the volume year is certain. 1938 Bulletin passage is two-column OCR; only used for the general point on Spanish-era keepers. Focal height 70 m = 231 ft converted. The 1921 hurricane and $4,375 fiscal-1922 repair line are matched by place/time, not stated as linked in the source. USLHS roster lines are as printed; Domingo Suarez-Rosa linked to the Bulletin's Suarez Rosa obituary by name plus Mona in its list of stations. Roster gap 1945-1959 is the archive's. Fact-check 2026-10-22: 1921 hurricane date (9 and 10 Sept) confirmed on the page image; Metz quote cannot be traced to a named original; Suarez Rosa obituary linked to the archive's Domingo Suarez-Rosa by name plus Mona in the Bulletin's station list only; Today section does not claim boat-only access (no source).
